title: T6 - Using analyzers
jupyter: python3

Analyzers are objects that do not change the behavior of a simulation, but just report on its internal state, almost always something to do with `sim.people`. This tutorial takes you through some of the built-in analyzers and gives a brief example of how to build your own.


<div class="alert alert-info">

Click [here](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/starsimhub/hpvsim/HEAD?urlpath=lab%2Ftree%2Fdocs%2Ftutorials%2Ftut_analyzers.ipynb) to open an interactive version of this notebook.

</div>


## Results by age

By far the most common reason to use an analyzer is to report results by age. The per-genotype and aggregate results in `sim.results` (e.g. `sim.results.hpvtotal.cancers`) use standardized age bins which may not match the age bins for available data on cervical cancers. The `AgeResults` analyzer lets you record any HPV result at the exact age bins and years you choose. You configure it with a `result_args` dictionary whose keys are the results you want by age; each entry lists the `years` to snapshot and the bin `edges`:

```{python}
#| collapsed: false
#| jupyter: {outputs_hidden: false}
#| tags: []
import numpy as np
import sciris as sc
import hpvsim as hpv

# A multi-decade run with a decent population size generates enough cancers to
# illustrate age-specific results.
age_analyzer = hpv.AgeResults(
    result_args=sc.objdict(
        # The keys are any per-age result of the HPV modules.
        hpv_prevalence=sc.objdict(
            years=[2019],  # The year(s) to generate results for
            edges=np.array([0., 15., 20., 25., 30., 40., 45., 50., 55., 65., 100.]),
        ),
        cancers=sc.objdict(
            years=[2019],
            edges=np.array([0., 20., 25., 30., 40., 45., 50., 55., 65., 100.]),
        ),
    )
)

sim = hpv.Sim(n_agents=20e3, genotypes=[16, 18], location='nigeria',
              start=1970, stop=2020, dt=1.0, analyzers=[age_analyzer])
sim.run()

a = sim.analyzers['ageresults']
hpv.plot_by_age(a, 'cancers')
```

The recorded values are also available as a tidy dataframe, which is the easiest way to line the model up against your own data (rows are the snapshot years, columns are the age bins):

```{python}
#| collapsed: false
#| jupyter: {outputs_hidden: false}
#| tags: []
a.to_dataframe(key='cancers')
```

To fit these age-specific outputs to observed data, pass the data to the `Calibration` object — see the [calibration tutorial](tut_calibration.qmd).

## Snapshots

A snapshot takes a "picture" of the `sim.people` object at specified points in time — a frozen deep copy you can inspect after the run. The following example snapshots the population and plots its age structure by sex at that moment:

```{python}
#| tags: []
snap = hpv.snapshot(timepoints=[2020])
sim = hpv.Sim(genotypes=[16, 18], location='nigeria',
              start=2000, stop=2020, dt=1.0, n_agents=20e3, analyzers=[snap])
sim.run()

# Retrieve the People snapshot taken in 2020.
people = sim.analyzers['snapshot'].get(2020)

import pylab as pl
alive = people.alive.values
ages = people.age.values[alive]
female = people.female.values[alive]

fig, ax = pl.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.hist([ages[female], ages[~female]], bins=np.arange(0, 90, 5),
        stacked=True, label=['Female', 'Male'])
ax.set_xlabel('Age')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of people')
ax.set_title('Population age structure in 2020')
ax.legend()
pl.show()
```

Because the snapshot is a deep copy, it is unaffected by anything that happens to `sim.people` later in the run — handy for comparing the population at two different times.

## Age pyramids

Age pyramids, like snapshots, take a picture of the people at a given point in time, and then bin them into age groups by sex. When you have a matching observed pyramid you can overlay it by passing `datafile=`:

```{python}
#| tags: []
# Make the age pyramid analyzer
age_pyr = hpv.age_pyramid(
    timepoints=[2010, 2020],
    edges=np.linspace(0, 100, 21))

# Make the sim, run, get the analyzer, and plot. HPVsim ships demographic
# data for any country in the UN World Population Prospects, so we can point
# the sim at a different location simply by name.
sim = hpv.Sim(location='south africa', start=2000, stop=2030, dt=0.5,
              n_agents=20e3, analyzers=[age_pyr])
sim.run()

a = sim.analyzers['age_pyramid']
a.plot()
```
